title: Wallet Compatibility — x402 docs (Advanced Concepts)
quote: Type A: Plain EOA — Raw ECDSA from the private key. Type B: Deployed smart account (ERC-4337) — EIP-1271 isValidSignature on the contract. Type C: Counterfactual smart account (ERC-6492) — EIP-1271 after the factory deploys it. Type D: ERC-7702 EOA, permissive delegate — EIP-1271 on the delegate, which accepts raw owner ECDSA. Type E: ERC-7702 EOA, strict delegate — requires a wrapped or prefixed format. [...] This requires the facilitator to set an allowlist of permitted factory addresses (eip6492AllowedFactories). Arbitrary factory calls are blocked by default to prevent attacker-controlled transaction injection. [...] Permit2 permitWitnessTransferFrom calls isValidSignature on the payer at settlement, and the Permit2 path does not deploy the wallet first. [...] x402 signs with signTypedData, which produces a raw 65-byte ECDSA signature that a strict delegate rejects.

title: ERC-6492: Signature Validation for Predeploy Contracts
quote: Contracts can sign verifiable messages via ERC-1271. However, if the contract is not deployed yet, ERC-1271 verification is impossible, as you cannot call the isValidSignature function on said contract. [...] magic bytes 0x6492649264926492649264926492649264926492649264926492649264926492 [...] concat(abi.encode((create2Factory, factoryCalldata, originalERC1271Signature), (address, bytes, bytes)), magicBytes) [...] If there is contract code at the address. If so perform ERC-1271 verification as usual by invoking isValidSignature

title: ERC-1271: Standard Signature Validation Method for Contracts
quote: Externally Owned Accounts (EOA) can sign messages with their associated private keys, but currently contracts cannot. We propose a standard way for any contracts to verify whether a signature on a behalf of a given contract is valid. [...] function isValidSignature(bytes32 _hash, bytes memory _signature) public view returns (bytes4 magicValue) [...] MUST return the bytes4 magic value 0x1626ba7e when function passes
